rationale: C12 plausibly supplied a material template for the child’s rejection of a minerals-support bill. Both memoranda describe government support at above-market prices, argue that it would stimulate production beyond genuine need, criticize assistance confined to one segment of the minerals industry, and contend that the measure would obstruct a sound industry-wide solution. C24 and C17 provide closely related lead-and-zinc policy background, but neither contains as close a parallel to the child’s operative argument against subsidies.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The substantial additions to supply would depress lead and zinc prices
shared_material.parent_excerpt: it would continue such purchases at prices considerably in excess of market price... require the Government to buy far greater quantities of these minerals than are necessary
shared_material.explanation: Both object to price-support machinery because it encourages mineral production beyond actual market or defense requirements.

shared_material.child_excerpt: approval of H.R. 8860 would generate demands for equal treatment and similar subsidies from other producers of lead and zinc as well as producers of many other minerals
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the provisions of H.R. 6373 would apply to only a small segment of the domestic minerals industry and would not reach the fundamentals of the problem
shared_material.explanation: Both reject selective federal assistance to a limited group of mineral producers as inequitable and inadequate.

shared_material.child_excerpt: it would harm rather than help the lead-zinc industry... increase the problems of lead-zinc producers
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Indeed this bill would make solution of the overall problems of the industry more difficult
shared_material.explanation: The central drafting move is the same: a nominally protective minerals measure is opposed on the ground that it would aggravate the industry’s underlying problems.

shared_material.child_excerpt: A lasting solution can best be achieved through a world-wide balance of production and consumption
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The interests of the domestic minerals industry will be better served by proceeding with the careful development of a long range minerals program than by approving a stopgap measure
shared_material.explanation: Each contrasts the proposed short-term intervention with a broader, durable solution based on industry-wide policy.
